question: Does this unit satisfy WCAG 2.2 1.1.1 in its applicable states?
method: Inspect each image, icon, canvas and chart with its accessible alternative.
pass_condition: Equivalent purpose/information survives nonvisual use; decorative content is ignored. Apply the complete linked criterion and its definitions; this checklist is not a substitute.
countercheck: Compare actual task meaning, not mere presence of an alt attribute.
recommendation: Provide contextual alternatives and structured chart data.

question: Does this unit satisfy WCAG 2.2 1.2.1 in its applicable states?
method: Play each prerecorded audio-only/video-only item and its alternative.
pass_condition: The alternative covers information and timing needed for the task. Apply the complete linked criterion and its definitions; this checklist is not a substitute.
countercheck: Check whether it is already a clearly labelled alternative for text.
recommendation: Supply a transcript or appropriate equivalent track.

question: Does this unit satisfy WCAG 2.2 1.2.2 in its applicable states?
method: Compare prerecorded video speech and meaningful sounds against captions.
pass_condition: Captions convey the relevant audio in sync. Apply the complete linked criterion and its definitions; this checklist is not a substitute.
countercheck: Check alternative-for-text exception and omitted speakers/sounds.
recommendation: Correct caption content and timing.

question: Does this unit satisfy WCAG 2.2 1.2.3 in its applicable states?
method: Compare visual-only information with description or media alternative.
pass_condition: The permitted alternative preserves meaningful visual information. Apply the complete linked criterion and its definitions; this checklist is not a substitute.
countercheck: Check whether the media is a labelled text alternative.
recommendation: Provide the missing descriptive alternative.

question: Does this unit satisfy WCAG 2.2 1.2.4 in its applicable states?
method: Observe a controlled live media session and caption stream.
pass_condition: Live synchronized audio has usable captions. Apply the complete linked criterion and its definitions; this checklist is not a substitute.
countercheck: Distinguish live media from prerecorded playback.
recommendation: Enable and verify live caption delivery.

question: Does this unit satisfy WCAG 2.2 1.2.5 in its applicable states?
method: Play prerecorded video without looking and compare description.
pass_condition: Meaningful visual information is available through audio description. Apply the complete linked criterion and its definitions; this checklist is not a substitute.
countercheck: Determine whether existing audio already conveys all relevant visuals.
recommendation: Add an audio description track.

question: Does this unit satisfy WCAG 2.2 1.3.1 in its applicable states?
method: Compare rendered groups, tables, headings and fields to the accessibility tree.
pass_condition: Relationships are programmatically available or available in text. Apply the complete linked criterion and its definitions; this checklist is not a substitute.
countercheck: Inspect nested and dynamically replaced structures.
recommendation: Use semantic structure and explicit relationships.

question: Does this unit satisfy WCAG 2.2 1.3.2 in its applicable states?
method: Read content in DOM/accessibility traversal order after responsive rearrangement.
pass_condition: Order preserves meaning. Apply the complete linked criterion and its definitions; this checklist is not a substitute.
countercheck: Compare the visual task sequence with nonvisual reading.
recommendation: Correct source order rather than only CSS positioning.

question: Does this unit satisfy WCAG 2.2 1.3.3 in its applicable states?
method: Execute instructions without shape, position, sound or color clues.
pass_condition: Instructions retain sufficient identification. Apply the complete linked criterion and its definitions; this checklist is not a substitute.
countercheck: Check equivalent textual references in context.
recommendation: Name controls and destinations explicitly.

question: Does this unit satisfy WCAG 2.2 1.3.4 in its applicable states?
method: Rotate supported displays and inspect orientation locks.
pass_condition: Content works in both orientations unless essential. Apply the complete linked criterion and its definitions; this checklist is not a substitute.
countercheck: Test genuine essentiality rather than design preference.
recommendation: Remove unnecessary orientation restrictions.

question: Does this unit satisfy WCAG 2.2 1.3.5 in its applicable states?
method: Inspect personal-data fields and their programmatic purposes.
pass_condition: Applicable input purposes are identifiable. Apply the complete linked criterion and its definitions; this checklist is not a substitute.
countercheck: Check whether the field concerns the user or another entity.
recommendation: Set correct purpose metadata.

question: Does this unit satisfy WCAG 2.2 1.4.1 in its applicable states?
method: Inspect status, charts and validation with color removed.
pass_condition: Information has an additional perceivable cue. Apply the complete linked criterion and its definitions; this checklist is not a substitute.
countercheck: Check labels, patterns and shape rather than assuming grayscale simulation proves accessibility.
recommendation: Add text or other redundant cues.

question: Does this unit satisfy WCAG 2.2 1.4.2 in its applicable states?
method: Open a controlled page with audio enabled and inspect stopping controls.
pass_condition: Autoplay audio beyond three seconds has the required independent control. Apply the complete linked criterion and its definitions; this checklist is not a substitute.
countercheck: Check actual duration and system versus page volume.
recommendation: Stop autoplay or expose independent audio controls.

question: Does this unit satisfy WCAG 2.2 1.4.3 in its applicable states?
method: Measure computed foreground/background contrast for each text state.
pass_condition: Applicable text meets 4.5:1, or 3:1 for qualifying large text; exceptions are evidenced. Apply the complete linked criterion and its definitions; this checklist is not a substitute.
countercheck: Inspect transparency, gradients, font metrics and inactive/logo exceptions.
recommendation: Adjust colors while preserving semantic meaning.

question: Does this unit satisfy WCAG 2.2 1.4.4 in its applicable states?
method: Resize text to 200 percent and execute the task.
pass_condition: Text resizes without lost content/function, subject to criterion exceptions. Apply the complete linked criterion and its definitions; this checklist is not a substitute.
countercheck: Test text scaling separately from viewport resizing.
recommendation: Use scalable text and flexible containers.

question: Does this unit satisfy WCAG 2.2 1.4.5 in its applicable states?
method: Inspect text embedded in images and available presentation controls.
pass_condition: Text is used where the presentation can be achieved with text, except permitted cases. Apply the complete linked criterion and its definitions; this checklist is not a substitute.
countercheck: Check essential branding and user customization exceptions.
recommendation: Render ordinary interface text as real text.

question: Does this unit satisfy WCAG 2.2 1.4.10 in its applicable states?
method: Test 320 CSS px width or 256 CSS px height as appropriate, including 400 percent zoom equivalence.
pass_condition: Reflow preserves functionality without two-axis scrolling except essential two-dimensional parts. Apply the complete linked criterion and its definitions; this checklist is not a substitute.
countercheck: Do not extend a table/map exception to surrounding controls or individual text cells.
recommendation: Reflow layouts and isolate necessary two-dimensional regions.

question: Does this unit satisfy WCAG 2.2 1.4.11 in its applicable states?
method: Measure component boundaries and meaningful graphics across states.
pass_condition: Required visual information meets 3:1 against adjacent colors, subject to exceptions. Apply the complete linked criterion and its definitions; this checklist is not a substitute.
countercheck: Distinguish decorative borders from information necessary to identify a control/state.
recommendation: Strengthen necessary state and graphical contrast.

question: Does this unit satisfy WCAG 2.2 1.4.12 in its applicable states?
method: Override line height to 1.5, paragraph spacing to 2, letter spacing to .12 and word spacing to .16 times font size.
pass_condition: Applicable content retains information and function. Apply the complete linked criterion and its definitions; this checklist is not a substitute.
countercheck: Check scripts/languages where a spacing property does not apply.
recommendation: Allow flexible text containers and wrapping.

question: Does this unit satisfy WCAG 2.2 1.4.13 in its applicable states?
method: Trigger hover/focus content, move into it, dismiss it and wait.
pass_condition: Additional content supports the criterion's dismissal, persistence and hover requirements. Apply the complete linked criterion and its definitions; this checklist is not a substitute.
countercheck: Check exceptions for browser-controlled content or non-obscuring content.
recommendation: Make custom popovers dismissible and persistent.

question: Does this unit satisfy WCAG 2.2 2.1.1 in its applicable states?
method: Complete all actions with keyboard alone, including custom widgets.
pass_condition: All applicable functionality is keyboard operable. Apply the complete linked criterion and its definitions; this checklist is not a substitute.
countercheck: Distinguish an essential input-path function from a mouse-only implementation.
recommendation: Provide keyboard equivalents.

question: Does this unit satisfy WCAG 2.2 2.1.2 in its applicable states?
method: Enter and leave each modal, editor, embedded region and menu with keyboard.
pass_condition: Focus can leave; nonstandard exit methods are disclosed. Apply the complete linked criterion and its definitions; this checklist is not a substitute.
countercheck: Try reverse traversal and the documented escape method.
recommendation: Repair focus containment and exits.

question: Does this unit satisfy WCAG 2.2 2.1.4 in its applicable states?
method: Type in content and inspect character-only shortcuts.
pass_condition: Shortcuts can be disabled/remapped or operate only on focused components. Apply the complete linked criterion and its definitions; this checklist is not a substitute.
countercheck: Check speech-input accidental activation and modifiers.
recommendation: Scope or configure shortcuts.

question: Does this unit satisfy WCAG 2.2 2.2.1 in its applicable states?
method: Trigger each time limit with controlled test data.
pass_condition: The required disable/adjust/extend option exists unless a criterion exception applies. Apply the complete linked criterion and its definitions; this checklist is not a substitute.
countercheck: Verify essential/live/long-duration exceptions from actual behavior.
recommendation: Allow adequate control of session timing.

question: Does this unit satisfy WCAG 2.2 2.2.2 in its applicable states?
method: Observe moving, blinking, scrolling and auto-updating content during another task.
pass_condition: Required pause/stop/hide or frequency controls work. Apply the complete linked criterion and its definitions; this checklist is not a substitute.
countercheck: Check the distinct conditions for motion versus auto-updates.
recommendation: Provide stable user-controlled presentation.

question: Does this unit satisfy WCAG 2.2 2.3.1 in its applicable states?
method: Inspect animation/video frame characteristics with an appropriate flash-analysis tool.
pass_condition: Flashes remain within the defined frequency or area/intensity thresholds. Apply the complete linked criterion and its definitions; this checklist is not a substitute.
countercheck: Do not expose a reviewer to suspected hazardous flashing; lack of analyzer remains unknown.
recommendation: Remove flashing or validate a safer replacement.

question: Does this unit satisfy WCAG 2.2 2.4.1 in its applicable states?
method: Use keyboard navigation and inspect bypass landmarks in the accessibility tree. Add screen-reader navigation only when explicitly requested.
pass_condition: A mechanism bypasses blocks repeated across multiple pages. Apply the complete linked criterion and its definitions; this checklist is not a substitute.
countercheck: Check focus placement after activation, not only link existence.
recommendation: Provide working skip navigation or equivalent structure.

question: Does this unit satisfy WCAG 2.2 2.4.2 in its applicable states?
method: Inspect browser/window titles across routes and states.
pass_condition: Titles distinguish topic or purpose. Apply the complete linked criterion and its definitions; this checklist is not a substitute.
countercheck: Check dynamically loaded views and duplicate titles.
recommendation: Set meaningful context-specific titles.

question: Does this unit satisfy WCAG 2.2 2.4.3 in its applicable states?
method: Record focus sequence through normal, error and modal states.
pass_condition: Traversal preserves meaning and operability. Apply the complete linked criterion and its definitions; this checklist is not a substitute.
countercheck: Check return focus after closing or deleting a focused item.
recommendation: Correct focus order and restoration.

question: Does this unit satisfy WCAG 2.2 2.4.4 in its applicable states?
method: Read each link with its programmatically determined context.
pass_condition: Destination purpose is determinable unless genuinely ambiguous for everyone. Apply the complete linked criterion and its definitions; this checklist is not a substitute.
countercheck: Check repeated generic labels and cards with multiple destinations.
recommendation: Clarify link text or associated context.

question: Does this unit satisfy WCAG 2.2 2.4.5 in its applicable states?
method: Find each page through available navigation mechanisms.
pass_condition: Multiple finding mechanisms exist except process/result exceptions. Apply the complete linked criterion and its definitions; this checklist is not a substitute.
countercheck: Do not mistake several links in one mechanism for independent ways.
recommendation: Add appropriate search, indexes or navigation.

question: Does this unit satisfy WCAG 2.2 2.4.6 in its applicable states?
method: Compare headings/labels with the actual content/action.
pass_condition: They describe topic or purpose. Apply the complete linked criterion and its definitions; this checklist is not a substitute.
countercheck: Check translated and repeated labels in their full context.
recommendation: Use specific task-oriented labels.

question: Does this unit satisfy WCAG 2.2 2.4.7 in its applicable states?
method: Traverse every interactive element without pointer input.
pass_condition: Keyboard focus is visibly identifiable. Apply the complete linked criterion and its definitions; this checklist is not a substitute.
countercheck: Check every theme and custom control, not selected-state styling alone.
recommendation: Provide a distinct visible focus indicator.

question: Does this unit satisfy WCAG 2.2 2.4.11 in its applicable states?
method: Traverse with sticky headers, footers, banners and open overlays.
pass_condition: Focused components are not entirely hidden by author-created content. Apply the complete linked criterion and its definitions; this checklist is not a substitute.
countercheck: Check scrolling and user-movable-content qualifications.
recommendation: Adjust scroll offsets and overlay behavior.

question: Does this unit satisfy WCAG 2.2 2.5.1 in its applicable states?
method: Execute multipoint/path gestures with a single pointer alternative.
pass_condition: Applicable functions do not require multipoint/path gestures. Apply the complete linked criterion and its definitions; this checklist is not a substitute.
countercheck: Check whether the path itself is essential.
recommendation: Provide simple pointer controls.

question: Does this unit satisfy WCAG 2.2 2.5.2 in its applicable states?
method: Press, move off target, release and undo with safe fixtures.
pass_condition: Pointer actions support the required cancellation/reversal behavior. Apply the complete linked criterion and its definitions; this checklist is not a substitute.
countercheck: Check essential down-event activation exceptions.
recommendation: Commit on release with cancellation or undo.

question: Does this unit satisfy WCAG 2.2 2.5.3 in its applicable states?
method: Compare visible control text to its accessible name.
pass_condition: Accessible name contains the visible label text. Apply the complete linked criterion and its definitions; this checklist is not a substitute.
countercheck: Check symbols and text presented as images.
recommendation: Align spoken and visible names.

question: Does this unit satisfy WCAG 2.2 2.5.4 in its applicable states?
method: Trigger motion-controlled actions and disable motion response.
pass_condition: An interface alternative and motion disabling are available unless excepted. Apply the complete linked criterion and its definitions; this checklist is not a substitute.
countercheck: Check supported-interface and essential exceptions.
recommendation: Provide ordinary controls for motion actions.

question: Does this unit satisfy WCAG 2.2 2.5.7 in its applicable states?
method: Complete each drag action through a single-pointer non-drag path.
pass_condition: Equivalent functionality is available unless essential or unmodified user-agent behavior. Apply the complete linked criterion and its definitions; this checklist is not a substitute.
countercheck: Test reorder, slider and canvas interactions independently.
recommendation: Add move buttons, menus or click-to-place actions.

question: Does this unit satisfy WCAG 2.2 2.5.8 in its applicable states?
method: Measure pointer targets and spacing in CSS pixels.
pass_condition: Targets meet 24 by 24 CSS pixels or a precisely evidenced spacing/equivalent/inline/agent/essential exception. Apply the complete linked criterion and its definitions; this checklist is not a substitute.
countercheck: Check hit area, not icon bounds; evaluate adjacent-target circles.
recommendation: Enlarge hit areas or separate controls.

question: Does this unit satisfy WCAG 2.2 3.1.1 in its applicable states?
method: Inspect programmatic default language; check screen-reader pronunciation only when explicitly requested.
pass_condition: The primary language is identifiable. Apply the complete linked criterion and its definitions; this checklist is not a substitute.
countercheck: Check localized route changes.
recommendation: Set correct language metadata.

question: Does this unit satisfy WCAG 2.2 3.1.2 in its applicable states?
method: Inspect passages in other languages and their language metadata.
pass_condition: Language changes are identifiable subject to stated exceptions. Apply the complete linked criterion and its definitions; this checklist is not a substitute.
countercheck: Check proper names, technical terms and indeterminate words.
recommendation: Mark language changes appropriately.

question: Does this unit satisfy WCAG 2.2 3.2.1 in its applicable states?
method: Focus every type of interactive element.
pass_condition: Receiving focus alone does not initiate a change of context. Apply the complete linked criterion and its definitions; this checklist is not a substitute.
countercheck: Separate allowed content updates from changes of context.
recommendation: Require activation for navigation or submission.

question: Does this unit satisfy WCAG 2.2 3.2.2 in its applicable states?
method: Change fields and selections individually.
pass_condition: Input does not unexpectedly change context without prior notice. Apply the complete linked criterion and its definitions; this checklist is not a substitute.
countercheck: Check documented select-to-navigate behavior.
recommendation: Use explicit submission or advance warning.

question: Does this unit satisfy WCAG 2.2 3.2.3 in its applicable states?
method: Compare repeated navigation across the application.
pass_condition: Relative order is consistent unless user initiated. Apply the complete linked criterion and its definitions; this checklist is not a substitute.
countercheck: Check intentional contextual additions separately.
recommendation: Reuse stable navigation ordering.

question: Does this unit satisfy WCAG 2.2 3.2.4 in its applicable states?
method: Compare components with the same function across views.
pass_condition: Identification remains consistent. Apply the complete linked criterion and its definitions; this checklist is not a substitute.
countercheck: Distinguish identical appearance with genuinely different functions.
recommendation: Unify functional names and icons.

question: Does this unit satisfy WCAG 2.2 3.2.6 in its applicable states?
method: Find recurring help mechanisms across pages.
pass_condition: Their relative order is consistent unless user initiated. Apply the complete linked criterion and its definitions; this checklist is not a substitute.
countercheck: Check the limited set of help mechanisms covered by the criterion.
recommendation: Place recurring help predictably.

question: Does this unit satisfy WCAG 2.2 3.3.1 in its applicable states?
method: Submit missing, malformed and conflicting values.
pass_condition: Detected errors identify the item and describe the problem in text. Apply the complete linked criterion and its definitions; this checklist is not a substitute.
countercheck: Check asynchronous/server-side validation and group errors.
recommendation: Associate actionable error text with fields.

question: Does this unit satisfy WCAG 2.2 3.3.2 in its applicable states?
method: Fill forms without relying on placeholders or trial-and-error.
pass_condition: Labels/instructions explain required input. Apply the complete linked criterion and its definitions; this checklist is not a substitute.
countercheck: Check units, formats, requirements and disappearing placeholders.
recommendation: Provide persistent labels and necessary instructions.

question: Does this unit satisfy WCAG 2.2 3.3.3 in its applicable states?
method: Trigger known correctable input errors.
pass_condition: Available correction suggestions are provided unless security/purpose prevents them. Apply the complete linked criterion and its definitions; this checklist is not a substitute.
countercheck: Distinguish a real protection need from generic implementation convenience.
recommendation: Offer specific safe correction guidance.

question: Does this unit satisfy WCAG 2.2 3.3.4 in its applicable states?
method: Simulate consequential legal, financial and user-data submissions.
pass_condition: At least the required reversal/check/confirmation protection exists. Apply the complete linked criterion and its definitions; this checklist is not a substitute.
countercheck: Use test records; check what is actually reversible.
recommendation: Add review, correction or reversal mechanisms.

question: Does this unit satisfy WCAG 2.2 3.3.7 in its applicable states?
method: Repeat a step requiring previously entered information in one process.
pass_condition: Redundant information is auto-populated or selectable unless excepted. Apply the complete linked criterion and its definitions; this checklist is not a substitute.
countercheck: Check essential, security and invalid-information exceptions.
recommendation: Carry data forward with explicit correction options.

question: Does this unit satisfy WCAG 2.2 3.3.8 in its applicable states?
method: Complete authentication including recovery and second factor.
pass_condition: Cognitive-function tests have the required alternative/assistance or applicable exception. Apply the complete linked criterion and its definitions; this checklist is not a substitute.
countercheck: Try paste, password managers and device-assisted routes; inspect every step.
recommendation: Support accessible authentication without forced memorization.

question: Does this unit satisfy WCAG 2.2 4.1.2 in its applicable states?
method: Inspect accessibility names, roles, values and state changes during interaction.
pass_condition: Required semantics are programmatically exposed and updated. Apply the complete linked criterion and its definitions; this checklist is not a substitute.
countercheck: Compare real accessibility tree and notifications to source attributes.
recommendation: Use native controls or correctly implement semantics.

question: Does this unit satisfy WCAG 2.2 4.1.3 in its applicable states?
method: Trigger search results, save status and validation without moving focus.
pass_condition: Applicable status messages are exposed to assistive technology. Apply the complete linked criterion and its definitions; this checklist is not a substitute.
countercheck: Check actual announcements and avoid conflating dialogs with status messages.
recommendation: Expose concise appropriate live status semantics.

question: Can users distinguish task groups without scanning every control?
method: Mark group boundaries on actual screenshots; compare layout tokens and nesting.
pass_condition: Grouping follows the task and related controls remain together.
countercheck: Try dense data, expanded sections and translated labels.
recommendation: Use alignment, proximity and restrained separation before adding decoration.

question: Does progressive disclosure reduce effort without hiding necessary decisions?
method: Walk first-use and expert tasks; record searches, reveals and lost context.
pass_condition: Necessary information is available at the decision point; secondary detail stays discoverable.
countercheck: Compare an expanded alternative; fewer visible controls can increase work.
recommendation: Move secondary detail behind labelled disclosure while retaining summaries.

question: Does spacing support reading and action at realistic data volumes?
method: Compare repeated rows, forms and panels at sparse and dense volumes.
pass_condition: Space communicates grouping and permits usable targets without gratuitous scrolling.
countercheck: Inspect compact expert workflows before recommending larger spacing.
recommendation: Derive spacing from the design system and task instead of universal pixel rules.

question: Is the next task-relevant action distinguishable from secondary actions?
method: Annotate attention competition in screenshots; execute the task without code hints.
pass_condition: Primary action, current state and content structure are understandable together.
countercheck: Check destructive-action prominence and multiple legitimate primary actions.
recommendation: Reduce competing emphasis and clarify action grouping.

question: Can users explain where they are and what scope an action affects?
method: Enter by deep link, search, dialog and restored session; inspect context indicators.
pass_condition: Location, selection scope and return path remain clear.
countercheck: Try similarly named records and nested overlays.
recommendation: Expose location, affected object and reliable return navigation.

question: Does the interface preserve attention across updates?
method: Observe sorting, refresh, pagination, selection and notifications.
pass_condition: Updates retain meaningful position and make changes understandable.
countercheck: Check intentional focus moves after explicit navigation.
recommendation: Preserve anchors and announce relevant changes.

question: Does typography distinguish roles while remaining readable?
method: Compare titles, body, metadata, errors and controls at supported scales.
pass_condition: Type roles are consistent and text is not clipped or visually confused.
countercheck: Check fallback fonts, scripts and actual rather than nominal weight.
recommendation: Use a small intentional type hierarchy and resilient fallback fonts.

question: Can the target audience scan and understand the actual text?
method: Read realistic long labels, paragraphs, numbers and dense tables in task order.
pass_condition: Formatting exposes distinctions, units and key information.
countercheck: Do not impose one line-length target on all scripts or data tables.
recommendation: Shorten unnecessary prose, group information and align comparable data.

question: Does localized content preserve meaning and structure?
method: Switch supported languages; test long strings, RTL, dates, amounts and plural forms.
pass_condition: Labels, units and ordering remain understandable without loss.
countercheck: Compare source translations to runtime formatting and mixed-direction input.
recommendation: Use locale-aware formatting and flexible text layouts.

question: Does color support the product's meaning consistently?
method: Compare semantic colors across all themes and control states.
pass_condition: Color meaning stays stable and decorative accents do not mask status.
countercheck: Check a brand accent reused for destructive actions.
recommendation: Separate semantic tokens from decorative brand colors.

question: Do details look intentional for the product and audience?
method: Compare spacing, icon families, surfaces, imagery and motion in real screens.
pass_condition: Visual decisions support a coherent recognizable product without distracting from work.
countercheck: Seek a simpler alternative; modernity is not a universal style or objective fact.
recommendation: Correct inconsistent details before adding ornament or redesigning the brand.

question: Does animation aid comprehension without obstructing interaction?
method: Repeat transitions with reduced-motion preferences and slow hardware.
pass_condition: Motion explains change and controls remain responsive; reduced mode is usable.
countercheck: Distinguish functional progress feedback from decorative movement.
recommendation: Use brief purposeful transitions and reduced-motion alternatives.

question: Do navigation categories follow user tasks rather than implementation modules?
method: Map goals to routes, menus and terminology; trace alternative entry points.
pass_condition: Related tasks are findable and categories have understandable boundaries.
countercheck: Try an unfamiliar role and cross-category task.
recommendation: Reorganize around audience tasks and provide cross-links where needed.

question: Can users find known and unfamiliar items with realistic data?
method: Try exact, partial, misspelled and empty searches plus filters/sorting.
pass_condition: Results and active constraints explain what is shown and how to recover.
countercheck: Check hidden filters, permission-scoped data and no-match versus no-data.
recommendation: Expose filters, useful empty states and clear recovery actions.

question: Do back, forward, reload, bookmarks and desktop reopen preserve expected context?
method: Exercise each supported navigation/history mechanism with nested views.
pass_condition: State and destination match the product contract without accidental data loss.
countercheck: Compare intended transient state with persisted state.
recommendation: Represent navigable state explicitly and restore meaningful context.

question: Do labels describe user outcomes rather than internal implementation?
method: Compare terms with audience documentation and actual actions.
pass_condition: Terms and icons have contextual meaning for the target audience.
countercheck: Treat reviewer familiarity as insufficient evidence of user understanding.
recommendation: Use audience vocabulary and label ambiguous icons.

question: Can users predict effects, scope and reversibility before acting?
method: Write predicted outcomes before executing unfamiliar actions; compare actual behavior.
pass_condition: Controls and feedback consistently support a coherent model.
countercheck: Test account/project/global scope and saved versus effective settings.
recommendation: Expose scope, persistence and consequence at the decision point.

question: Does the task require avoidable recall or mental transformation?
method: Record information carried between views, conversions and repeated decisions.
pass_condition: Necessary context is available when needed without redundant cognitive work.
countercheck: Compare expert shortcuts and novices; fewer clicks may hide more thinking.
recommendation: Keep contextual summaries and recognizable choices available.

question: Can representative users complete core goals with reasonable effort?
method: Walk first success, routine work and a complex task; record steps, waits and recovery.
pass_condition: The path is coherent and avoids unnecessary decisions or repeated entry.
countercheck: Compare an alternative path; do not equate shortest path with lowest effort.
recommendation: Remove redundant decisions while keeping necessary safeguards.

question: Can users cancel, undo and safely resume work?
method: Interrupt forms, bulk operations and dialogs using test data.
pass_condition: Control options preserve useful work and explain irreversible boundaries.
countercheck: Check partial completion and multi-step undo semantics.
recommendation: Offer predictable cancel, undo and resumable drafts.

question: Does feedback distinguish pending, success and failure?
method: Trigger fast, delayed and failed operations; record input/output timing.
pass_condition: Feedback reflects actual state and prevents accidental duplicate work.
countercheck: Compare optimistic UI with eventual server outcome.
recommendation: Tie feedback to operation lifecycle and allow safe retry.

question: Are empty, loading, partial, stale, error and permission states meaningful?
method: Force each reachable state through fixture data or approved mocks.
pass_condition: States explain the situation and present appropriate next actions.
countercheck: Check offline/denied versus truly empty data and partial success.
recommendation: Design distinct state messages with recovery paths.

question: Do unusual sequences preserve a coherent experience?
method: Rapidly change selection, navigate back, cancel and retry controlled operations.
pass_condition: Late responses do not overwrite newer intent or misrepresent completion.
countercheck: Vary response order and restart with existing data.
recommendation: Cancel stale work, reconcile state and retain user intent.

question: Can users recover without losing valid work?
method: Trigger validation, disconnection and expired-session paths with test data.
pass_condition: Recovery retains appropriate input and identifies what to do next.
countercheck: Check sensitive-data retention policy and retried duplicate submissions.
recommendation: Preserve safe drafts, clarify errors and make retries idempotent.

question: Do shared components behave and look consistently in their real contexts?
method: Compare a component-state matrix across screens and themes with token definitions.
pass_condition: Equivalent functions share relevant semantics, interaction and visual rules.
countercheck: Inspect overrides, nested instances and generated components.
recommendation: Repair shared causes and document justified variants.

question: Does the application respect supported platform conventions?
method: Exercise menus, shortcuts, window lifecycle, file pickers and system preferences.
pass_condition: Platform behavior is predictable for intended users.
countercheck: Do not force web conventions onto native controls or vice versa.
recommendation: Use platform conventions unless a task-specific exception is evidenced.

question: Do documented promises, design rules and actual behavior agree?
method: Trace a stated UI contract through configuration, shared code and runtime.
pass_condition: Supported variants implement the same declared contract or disclose a valid exception.
countercheck: Check stale docs and feature flags before calling behavior a defect.
recommendation: Align documentation and implementation at the source of truth.

question: Does the product remain usable at all declared window sizes and scale factors?
method: Sweep supported minimum/maximum sizes and breakpoints plus adjacent values.
pass_condition: Controls remain reachable and meaningful content is not accidentally lost.
countercheck: Test nested panes, dialogs, multiple monitors and OS scaling separately.
recommendation: Use resilient constraints and accessible overflow strategies.

question: Does adaptation honor preferences without breaking tasks?
method: Test supported themes, forced colors, reduced motion and input modalities.
pass_condition: Content and interaction remain perceivable and operable.
countercheck: Verify preferences are effective rather than merely selectable.
recommendation: Use semantic tokens and native preference APIs.

question: Does layout adapt to content extremes and dynamic updates?
method: Use zero, one and many items; long names; large numbers; streamed updates.
pass_condition: Users can navigate, compare and act without clipping or misleading summaries.
countercheck: Check virtualization and selection outside the visible range.
recommendation: Provide stable scalable lists and intentional truncation with full access.

question: Can users complete whole tasks with supported assistive technology?
method: Optional extension, only when explicitly requested: run core journeys with the declared browser/OS/screen-reader combination. Otherwise record an evidenced scope exclusion under M6.
pass_condition: Task meaning, relationships and feedback are available end to end.
countercheck: An automated scan or accessibility-tree dump alone cannot prove this.
recommendation: Fix barriers in the real interaction sequence and retest on supported combinations.

question: Does native software expose useful accessibility services?
method: Inspect platform accessibility trees, actions, values and notifications.
pass_condition: Native controls provide the information and actions needed by platform assistive technology.
countercheck: Check custom canvas controls and closed functionality explicitly.
recommendation: Use platform accessibility APIs and WCAG2ICT mapping with stated limits.

question: Is perceived simplicity supported by audience evidence?
method: Separate observed friction from user-reported comprehension and workload.
pass_condition: Claims are bounded to the tested audience/tasks; unknown perception remains a hypothesis.
countercheck: Ask a fresh evaluator to find a plausible contrary interpretation.
recommendation: Prefer changes that reduce confusion before visual novelty.

question: Does the interface make consequential state and intent credible?
method: Compare displayed progress, data freshness, permissions and destructive actions to actual outcomes.
pass_condition: The interface does not mislead about what happened or who controls the choice.
countercheck: Check hidden defaults, dark patterns and partial failures.
recommendation: Explain consequences honestly and make choices reversible where possible.

question: Do real-user observations support claims about success, effort and satisfaction?
method: When authorized, run representative tasks and collect completion/errors plus participant feedback.
pass_condition: Results report audience, conditions, sample and uncertainty; no invented ratings.
countercheck: Separate think-aloud effects, learning effects and participant claims from observer inference.
recommendation: Use observed recurring barriers to prioritize; validate changes with comparable tasks.

question: Does window restoration keep work reachable after monitor or scaling changes?
method: Move and resize a test window, restart, remove its former monitor or change scaling, then reopen.
pass_condition: Window and critical controls remain reachable; platform-managed placement is acceptable.
countercheck: Try persisted split widths and an offscreen former position.
recommendation: Clamp restored geometry to available displays and retain access to collapsed panels.

question: Do platform editing commands preserve object semantics?
method: Exercise copy/paste, undo, multiple selection, context menu and drag alternative on applicable objects.
pass_condition: Menu, keyboard and pointer routes produce equivalent appropriate results.
countercheck: Repeat with text-field focus and mixed selection.
recommendation: Use platform editing conventions and accessible alternatives to dragging.

question: Does first use deliver a real reusable result?
method: Start with a fresh disposable profile; complete the core task and reopen or export the created object.
pass_condition: A usable result exists beyond a demonstration or setup success indicator.
countercheck: Skip optional personalization and repeat without coaching.
recommendation: Center first use on the first meaningful result with contextual help.

question: Are denied and deferred permissions recoverable?
method: Trigger a required permission in context, deny it, retry later and compare with never-requested state.
pass_condition: Purpose and consequences are clear; available alternatives and recovery remain reachable.
countercheck: Restart after denial and after interrupted setup.
recommendation: Ask at point of need and explain the path to grant access later.

question: Does setup preserve progress and respect established users?
method: Interrupt each distinct setup exit state, restart, skip optional help and open an upgraded existing profile.
pass_condition: Necessary progress survives; optional steps do not trap users; established work remains available.
countercheck: Locate help again and repeat the first task independently.
recommendation: Persist meaningful progress and distinguish omitted help from missing prerequisites.

question: Can users find preferences through task language?
method: Classify all settings versus session choices, commands and system settings; attempt three product-specific lookup tasks.
pass_condition: Placement and labels match user tasks; navigation complexity is justified by content.
countercheck: Try narrow window, synonymous query and a second entry point.
recommendation: Group by familiar tasks; add search only where volume warrants it.

question: Does settings search lead to the precise actionable option?
method: Search name, help term and everyday synonym; open a hit in a collapsed group and return.
pass_condition: Target is visible and focused; query, filters and position remain intelligible.
countercheck: Use no-result query, active filter and disabled target.
recommendation: Expose location, resettable filters and an accessible reason for disabled values.

question: Does each settings control explain value, type and effect?
method: Inspect label, units, bounds, current value and control role; use keyboard to enter valid and invalid values.
pass_condition: Control semantics fit the decision; current value and effect are understandable.
countercheck: Use long labels and inspect accessible roles/states; distinguish a command from a persistent switch. Add a screen reader only when explicitly requested.
recommendation: Choose familiar controls and concise effect descriptions; preview sensory changes when useful.

question: Do setup and regular settings share the actual effective preference?
method: Change the same value through setup and regular settings, use the affected feature, restart and reset.
pass_condition: Displayed, persisted and effective values agree or a delayed application is explicitly explained.
countercheck: Cancel grouped edits and simulate failed saving in the disposable environment.
recommendation: Use one preference source and show the last effective value after failure.

question: Are overrides, defaults and unavailable resources understandable?
method: Compare device/user/project scope if present, remove an override and disconnect a selected test resource.
pass_condition: Effective value, origin and fallback are clear; resetting preferences preserves unrelated user content.
countercheck: Restore resource and verify the actual task result; compare another project and unchanged preference.
recommendation: Expose scope and fallback and separate preference reset from content deletion.
